To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the metabolomics of plasma and acyl-coa liver compounds can be used for the detection of intestinal neoplastic progression in ApcMin/+/+ mice and the development of therapeutic strategies.

high-throughput mass-spectrometry metabolomics combined with statistical analysis and pathway/network modeling can be used to identify metabolic signatures and metabolic pathway alterations in the host, which may be used for the development of novel diagnostic and therapeutic interventions.
high-fat diet in the ApcMin/+ model of intestinal cancer progression results in distinct plasma metabolic profiles, which are associated with the formation of intestinal polyps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel methods and approaches for the analysis of metabolomics data and the integration of metabolomics with other omics approaches.

the elucidation of the metabolic basis of intestinal cancer progression and the development of therapeutic strategies based on the identification of novel targets in the metabolic network of the host.
the elucidation of the role of diet in the pathogenesis of colon cancer, with the aim to identify new targets for the development and testing of preventive strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the high-throughput metabolomic approach is useful to monitor and infer the metabolic changes and interactions of the host under the controlled experimental conditions.
the metabolome is a useful tool to monitor and understand the impact of dietary and genetic factors on intestinal carcinogenesis.
metabolome profiling of plasma and liver acyl-CoAs of ApcMin+/+ mice fed with high-fat diet is a promising approach to identify biomarkers for intestinal neoplasms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of high throughput metabolomics with appropriate statistical modeling can be used to identify and infer changes and interaction in the metabolome of the host under experimental conditions.
the metabolic signatures of polyposis can be identified by metabolomics, and that the metabolic pathways of polyposes and intestinal cancer can be inferred by functional metabolomics.
high-fat diet in ApcMin/+/ mice is associated with changes in plasma and acyl CoA metabolite profiles, which in turn are associated with increased polyp formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
metabolomics can be used as a useful tool to monitor the impact of dietary interventions and genetic susceptibility to intestinal neoplasias.
the metabolic signature in the plasma of mice with polyposis is distinct from the wild-type and is further altered by diet.

high-throughput untargeted metabolomics can be used as a tool to identify and monitor metabolic signatures of intestinal neoplastic progression in mice and that the identified metabolites can be used as biomarkers for early detection of colorectal cancer.
